Change c0357. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. II; 1831 Ch. XIX.

Context before (unchanged): In this expedition we did not intend to follow the great road to Edinburgh, but to visit Windsor, Oxford, Matlock, and the Cumberland lakes, resolving to arrive at the completion of this tour about the end of July.

1818 text: I packed my chemical instruments, and the materials I had collected, resolving to finish my labours in some obscure nook in the northern highlands of Scotland.

1831 text: I packed up my chemical instruments, and the materials I had collected, resolving to finish my labours in some obscure nook in the northern highlands of Scotland.

Diff: I packed {+up+} my chemical instruments, and the materials I had collected, resolving to finish my labours in some obscure nook in the northern highlands of Scotland.

Context after (unchanged): We quitted London on the 27th of March, and remained a few days at Windsor, rambling in its beautiful forest.

result.rationale: The only change is the added phrasal verb "up" in "I packed up my chemical instruments", a colloquial idiom that keeps the meaning and events unchanged.
